requirements.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations.
requirements.summary: A persistent logrotate rule specifies daily rotation, seven retained copies, and compression; the installed legacy logrotate parser accepted it, the daily cron runner exists, and a forced rotation produced a valid compressed archive. The rule and parser result remained healthy after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A descriptor opened before rotation successfully wrote afterward. The active log retained its inode under copytruncate, and the post-rotation write appeared in the active file while prior content appeared in the compressed rotation.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on the managed Ubuntu 7.10 image with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic before and after execution. Its already-installed logrotate accepted and executed the configuration successfully; no package installation or platform upgrade occurred.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the node became temporarily unavailable, a different boot identity was observed, and cron, configuration, current and rotated data, kernel, and write health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot change.
limitations: Daily scheduling and seven-generation retention were validated through accepted configuration, the daily cron runner, and one forced rotation; the evidence window did not span seven natural daily cycles.
Failed-service collection was unsupported on this pre-systemd platform, although the relevant cron process and log behavior were directly verified before and after restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear task or evidence roles: installing the required rule (cmd-9a419e4ad5024698), performing a bounded forced-rotation/open-descriptor test (cmd-c4a3995c896f45a4), writing health markers (cmd-aa5e1ad24b3e4a17 and cmd-b5b32c54f8664db2), and carrying out the required restart (cmd-fa34202efd8f4575). No unnecessary mutation was identified. The temporary status and reboot-log files did not remain in the final bounded /tmp inventory, and lifecycle comparisons show no package-health, socket, or platform regression.
